title: E-Commerce Delivery Analytics
tagline: Use DuckDB SQL on 100k Brazilian orders to measure late deliveries - without inflating your KPIs.
question: How often do Olist deliveries arrive late, and how much does lateness hurt review scores?
audience: Students practising SQL joins and aggregations on a real multi-table dataset.
prerequisites: Free Kaggle account for real data

expected_runtime.real: ~10 seconds once the CSVs are in data/raw/

source.name: Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist
source.citation: Olist and André Sionek (2018). Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist. Kaggle. https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce
manual_steps: Sign in to Kaggle and open the dataset page.
Click Download to get archive.zip (~45 MB).
Upload the ZIP on this page, or run: python load_data.py --import path/to/archive.zip

lesson.title: Rows are not orders
lesson.summary: Orders have many items and sometimes several reviews. Joining them before aggregating multiplies rows and skews order-level metrics. Document each table's grain, aggregate children to one row per order, and check distinct order counts after every join.

challenges.title: Late rate by state
challenges.description: Join olist_customers_dataset.csv and compute late rate by customer_state.
challenges.outcome: A ranked chart of states with order counts.

challenges.title: Predict late delivery
challenges.description: Build features known at purchase time (estimated days, freight, seller) and train a classifier.
challenges.outcome: ROC AUC on a time-based holdout.

challenges.title: Seller scorecard
challenges.description: Aggregate items to seller grain and rank sellers by late share (min 30 orders).
challenges.outcome: A table that counts each order once per seller.
